A.explanation: Gives $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{2}$, which has inverted powers of $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ and does not match force times distance.

B.explanation: Gives $\text{kg s}^{-2}$, which is missing the length terms from both the newton and the extra distance.

C.explanation: Gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, which is the SI base units for force alone, before multiplying by distance.

D.explanation: Gives $\text{kg m}^{2} \text{s}^{-2}$, which is force $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ multiplied by distance $\text{m}$.

hints: Start from what moment of a force means: force multiplied by perpendicular distance, so the unit starts as $\text{N m}$.
Break the newton into SI base units using $F = ma$, which gives mass in $\text{kg}$ times acceleration in $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
Multiply those force base units by one more $\text{m}$ for distance and add the powers of $\text{m}$ together.
walkthrough: Moment of a force $=$ force $\times$ perpendicular distance, so its derived unit is $\text{N m}$.
Write force in base units from $F = ma$: mass is $\text{kg}$ and acceleration is $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Multiply by distance in $\text{m}$: $\text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = \text{kg m}^{2} \text{s}^{-2}$.
Check against the options: only one option has $\text{m}^{2}$ with $\text{kg}$ and $\text{s}^{-2}$.
